name: Non-familial Restrictive Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Evidence of impaired ventricular filling with normal or near-normal systolic function on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Marked biatrial enlargement on imaging studies
Exclusion of other causes of restrictive physiology such as constrictive pericarditis or infiltrative cardiomyopathies
Hemodynamic evidence of restrictive filling pattern on cardiac catheterization
Endomyocardial biopsy showing myocardial fibrosis without infiltrative or storage disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diastolic dysfunction with biatrial enlargement and exclusion of other causes of restrictive physiology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive imaging and exclusion of infiltrative or familial causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated jugular venous pressure with prominent y descent
searchTerms: high neck vein pressure with deep dip
raised neck vein pressure with y descent

pathognomonic.symptomName: Kussmaul's sign (paradoxical rise in jugular venous pressure on inspiration)
searchTerms: neck vein pressure rises on breathing in
paradoxical jugular vein increase with inspiration
abnormal neck vein pressure during breath
heart filling problems seen on ultrasound

common.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to elevated left atrial pressure
Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema from right heart failure
searchTerms: peripheral edema due to right heart failure

common.symptomName: Ascites secondary to systemic venous congestion
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from vein congestion
belly swelling due to blood backup
swollen liver due to chronic fluid backup
shortness of breath when lying down
difficulty breathing flat due to lung fluid

rare.symptomName: Thromboembolic events secondary to atrial enlargement
searchTerms: blood clots from enlarged heart chamber
clot events due to atrial dilation
electrical heart block treated with pacemaker

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP or NT-proBNP)
Absence of markers for infiltrative diseases (e.g., negative serum amyloid)
imaging: Echocardiography showing restrictive filling pattern with normal ventricular size and preserved systolic function
Cardiac MRI demonstrating biatrial enlargement and myocardial fibrosis without infiltration
Chest X-ray showing pulmonary venous congestion
genetic: No known pathogenic mutations associated with familial restrictive cardiomyopathy
other: Hemodynamic catheterization showing elevated ventricular filling pressures with normal systolic function
Endomyocardial biopsy revealing myocardial fibrosis without amyloid or storage material

distinguishingFeatures: Pericardial thickening or calcification on imaging
History of pericardial disease or surgery
Characteristic low voltage ECG with thickened ventricular walls
Systemic involvement such as neuropathy or nephrotic syndrome

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms despite therapy
Recurrent syncope or documented ventricular arrhythmias
Evidence of systemic infiltrative disease or malignancy
references: Maron BJ, Towbin JA, Thiene G, et al. Contemporary definitions and classification of the cardiomyopathies: an American Heart Association Scientific Statement. Circulation. 2006;113(14):1807-1816.
